themes.topic: Hierarchical structuring of śrāddha timing by capacity

mentions.quote: Now, the time for ancestral rites (śrāddhakāla).
For one who is unable, Gautama says: 'Or from Pañcamī onwards of the dark fortnight.'
If one is even less able, Manu says:
If one is unable to do even this, Devala says it should be done four times in the middle of the year.

themes.justification: The entire window organises śrāddha time-determinations in a cascade of decreasing stringency (from daily to annual), making capacity-based hierarchy the central structural principle.

themes.topic: Digest harmonisation of conflicting smṛti authorities

mentions.quote: Because if in the verse of Manu, tarpaṇa were taken by the word pitṛyajña, the name piṇḍānvāhāryaka would be impossible.
And thus, in the Brahma Purāṇa and Viṣṇudharmottara, the three stated are those of winter and the cool season, other than the dark Aṣṭamī of Phālguna.
Therefore, from the sight of both verses, the option is proper, and it is a structured one.

themes.justification: The Vīramitrodaya systematically reconciles divergent rulings from Manu, Kātyāyana, the Purāṇas, and nibandha authors through Mīmāṃsā reasoning, characterising the text as a digest (nibandha).

themes.topic: Mīmāṃsā hermeneutics applied to ritual injunctions

mentions.quote: For that is a name by the tatprakhyanyāya (the Mīmāṃsā maxim of naming from a prominent feature).
Since an obligatory (nitya) rite has no fruit, there is no hierarchy of fruit. Rather, it is a structured option based on capacity.
as in the case of the holding of the sixteenth cup (ṣoḍaśigrahaṇa), it is proper to infer a greater abundance of fruit.

themes.justification: The author repeatedly deploys Mīmāṃsā categories (tatprakhyanyāya, nitya vs. kāmya, vīpsā, syntactical unity) to resolve ritual ambiguities, making Mīmāṃsā hermeneutics the operative interpretive framework.

themes.topic: Distinction between obligatory (nitya) and optional (kāmya) śrāddha

mentions.quote: And this is obligatory (nitya), from the statement of Kātyāyana: 'One should not transgress the dark fortnight, even with vegetables.'
And it is also optional (kāmya).
The sixteen days that are stated as the time for the śrāddha, they apply to another, optional (kāmya) śrāddha

themes.justification: The nitya/kāmya distinction recurs at p-91785d, p-173625, and p-03096d, structuring the normative evaluation of whether a given śrāddha performance is required or supererogatory.

themes.topic: Lunar and solar astronomy as the framework for ritual timing

mentions.quote: At an eclipse of the moon and sun, at a partial rising, or on the Kapilaṣaṣṭhī
In the eighth part of Caturdaśī, the moon becomes waning. In the eighth part of Amāvāsyā, it is said to become a particle again.
The four-times-a-year option is when the sun is in Virgo, Aquarius, Taurus, and Libra

themes.justification: From solar ingresses (Virgo) to tithis to the waning of the moon, the entire window is organised around an astronomical calendar that determines when rites must, may, or may not be performed.

themes.topic: Social differentiation in ritual eligibility (varṇa, gender, fire-status)

mentions.quote: one who has established the sacred fires should take Sinīvālī; for one without fires, etc., Kuhū is remembered

since such a thing is possible only for one who maintains the sacred fires (sāgnika), who is entitled to the Piṇḍapitṛyajña, this verse … applies only to him, not to all

themes.justification: The text systematically differentiates rules based on the performer's fire-maintaining status (sāgnika vs. niragnika), varṇa (Brahmin, Śūdra), and gender, showing social stratification as a governing variable in ritual law.

citations.quote: This is from the statement of Nārada in the Pṛthvīcandrodaya.
citations.justification: Nārada is cited via the Pṛthvīcandrodaya at p-3c35e5 for the examination of prohibited tithi etc. in a single Mahālaya performance.

citations.quote: The same is stated by Vṛddhagārgya:
citations.justification: Cited at p-b1c8e1 for the prohibition of śrāddha in Prājāpatya, Pauṣṇa, and ancestral nakṣatras and on Bhārgava's day.

citations.quote: By this statement of Marīci
citations.justification: Marīci is cited at p-1563aa for the Caturdaśī rule specifying who (those killed by poison, snake, beast, fire, wild animal, or Brahmin) may have śrāddha on Caturdaśī.

citations.quote: This is from the statement of Kārṣṇājini.
citations.justification: Kārṣṇājini is cited at p-85c175 for the rule that in daily Mahālaya śrāddha, Nandā and Caturdaśī need not be avoided.

citations.quote: the word 'one who has established the sacred fires' here is also indicative of one who maintains the smārta fire, says the Madanapārijāta.
citations.justification: The Madanapārijāta is cited at p-3890bd as an interpretive authority extending the sāgnika category to smārta-fire maintainers for purposes of Sinīvālī/Kuhū determination.

citations.quote: Because of this statement of Devala, a śrāddha is enjoined there as well.
citations.justification: Devala is cited at p-8b1a84 for the statement that the bright Pratipad with the sixteen days has the nature of Darśa and merits śrāddha, and earlier for reduced-schedule options.

citations.quote: The sense of the Gobhilabhāṣya and Śabara is also thus.
citations.justification: The Gobhilabhāṣya is co-cited with Śabara at p-bf2918 to support the rule for partial-pervasion determination in Amāvāsyā timing.

citations.quote: The sense of the Gobhilabhāṣya and Śabara is also thus.
citations.justification: Śabara's Mīmāṃsā commentary is invoked at p-bf2918 for the determination of partial-pervasion of the Amāvāsyā tithi.

citations.quote: And that is not the tarpaṇa in the form of the pitṛyajña that is part of the five great sacrifices, as stated by Medhātithi, because since that is accomplished by concomitance on the day of the śrāddha, an injunction of its being after that is impossible.
citations.justification: Medhātithi's interpretation is explicitly refuted at p-317990, where his identification of tarpaṇa with the five-great-sacrifice pitṛyajña is rejected on logical grounds.

citations.quote: says the author of the Pariśiṣṭaprakāśa
citations.justification: Cited at p-0cff55 and p-4fbead for interpretive rulings on Amāvāsyā timing applicability and on the full-moon-ending nature of Jyeṣṭha and Mārgaśīrṣa.
